name: JewelHuntrix scrap-metal ruleset
description: Precious-metal melt-value ruleset. This is INDEPENDENT from jewelhuntrix-brands.json (the maker/design-value path). Use routing_logic below to decide which path (or both) applies to a given listing.

risk_budget.principle: Scrap-path pieces cannot be confirmed from a Vinted listing alone - true weight and true purity are only certain once the piece is at home and can be weighed, magnet-tested, or otherwise checked. Until then this is a bet on the seller's stated hallmark and an estimated/unconfirmed weight. The max_total_cost caps how much of that unconfirmed bet you're willing to place per item.
risk_budget.shipping_reference_note: Jewelry shipping on Vinted is typically up to about EUR 3.50 - this is already included in the 10.00 cap, it is not an additional allowance on top.
risk_budget.meaning_of_the_cap: asking_price + shipping_cost must be <= 10.00 EUR for a scrap_path listing to be worth buying on suspicion alone, BEFORE in-hand confirmation.
risk_budget.what_this_is_not: This is NOT a value/profit threshold and NOT a replacement for the melt_value_formula comparison. A listing can pass this cap and still be a bad buy if melt value (once weight is confirmed) turns out lower than price. The cap only answers: 'is the unconfirmed risk small enough to take a chance on this item sight-unseen-in-hand?'
risk_budget.app_behavior: If asking_price + shipping_cost > 10.00 EUR for a scrap_path (hallmark-confirmed-from-photo-only, weight-unconfirmed) listing, do not surface it as a buy candidate regardless of how good the melt-value estimate looks - the estimate is still unverified and the money at risk is too high for an unconfirmed bet. Once weight IS genuinely confirmed (seller-stated and credible, not estimated), this cap no longer applies and the normal melt_value_formula / underpriced_signal logic in scoring_notes takes over instead.

routing_logic.principle: A brand/attribution signal and a hallmark signal are two separate, non-exclusive value paths. Never let one path's absence suppress the other.

rules.condition: listing/photos show a maker name, signature, or strong construction attribution (see jewelhuntrix-brands.json) and NO precious-metal hallmark
rules.note: Material is often base metal or plastic. Do not run scrap valuation - it will return ~0 and wrongly suppress the score.

rules.condition: listing/photos show a precious-metal hallmark (925/800/999/375/585/750/916/950/900/Plat/PT) and NO maker name or attribution signal
rules.note: Value is melt-value driven. Brand attribution effort is wasted here - go straight to weight + purity + spot price.

rules.condition: both a maker/attribution signal AND a precious-metal hallmark are present
rules.note: Score both paths independently and take the higher estimate. A signed 14k/18k piece by a recognised maker can be worth more as a collectible than as scrap, or vice versa if condition is poor - never average the two, take the max.
Not enough information to value via either path. Do not fabricate a score.

silver.note: 925/sterling is by far the most common in costume + fine jewelry. 800 common in older European pieces. 999 is investment/fine silver, rare in jewelry.

gold.note: 9k/375 common in UK/older European gold. 14k/585 common in US. 18k/750 common in Europe/Middle East fine jewelry. 22k/916 common in Indian/Middle Eastern gold.

platinum.note: Heavy, white, does not tarnish - a quick physical tell alongside the stamp. Less common than gold/silver in costume jewelry contexts, more common in fine jewelry.

non_solid_warnings.effect: NOT solid precious metal. Do not apply full purity_map melt calculation.

handling.gold_filled: Contains a bonded layer of gold (commonly 1/20th of total weight by law in the US). Has SOME scrap value but far below solid gold - use a fractional estimate (~5% of total weight as gold content) only if you must estimate, and flag as approximate.
handling.plated_rolled: Plating/rolled layer is microscopically thin. Scrap value is negligible - route to brand_path or unscored, not scrap_path.
handling.vermeil: Gold plating over sterling silver base - value the silver base only via scrap_path (verify the base is actually sterling), ignore the gold plating for melt purposes.

french_system.note: France uses poincons (guarantee stamps) instead of / alongside numeric marks.

marks.boar_head: silver guarantee, older mark (hure de sanglier)
marks.owl: import/small-work guarantee mark, various purities - verify alongside a numeric or maker mark (chouette)

spot_price.update_policy: Spot prices move daily/hourly. Do NOT hardcode a static number as ground truth in the app. Fetch or manually refresh regularly (recommend: daily) from a live source (e.g. LBMA-based feed, a price API, or manual entry) before running any melt-value calculation.

reference_values_at_time_of_writing.note: For orientation only - replace with a live/refreshed value before use.
reference_values_at_time_of_writing.as_of: 2026-08 (approximate, silver only - fetch current gold/platinum before use)

example.scenario: 50cm sterling silver necklace, weight unknown in listing

weight_handling.principle: Weight in grams is the single most common missing variable in listings. Never silently assume a weight to force a score.

fallback_options: Estimate a rough low/high range from visible chain/piece thickness and style in photos (label clearly as an estimate range, not a point value)
Flag listing for manual weight request to seller before computing a melt-value score
Surface listing as '<metal> <purity> - weight unconfirmed' in results rather than a false-precision numeric score

scoring_notes.melt_value_is_a_floor: Melt value is the minimum defensible value (scrap/bullion floor), not a resale ceiling. An intact, wearable piece can and often does sell above melt value for styling/wearability/brand reasons - do not cap a listing's estimated resale value at melt value.
scoring_notes.underpriced_signal: Flag as a strong buy signal when: asking_price (incl. shipping) < melt_value_at_current_spot, with weight confirmed (not estimated).
scoring_notes.do_not_flag_on_estimated_weight: If weight was estimated (not confirmed from listing/seller), do not auto-flag as underpriced - surface for manual review only.

quick_physical_tests.method: hold a strong magnet to the piece
quick_physical_tests.read: gold/silver/platinum/brass/copper are non-magnetic. Strong magnetic pull = base metal or steel, likely plated fake regardless of stamp.
solid precious metal feels dense and cool. Suspiciously light for its size suggests hollow/plated/base metal.
crisp, correctly-shaped stamp vs mushy/blurred/wrong-shaped stamp (possible fake hallmark).
